sentences: Orthogonal Vectors asks whether two Boolean vector collections contain a pair with no coordinate where both vectors have a one.
The selected question concerns an essentially linear-time algorithm for this problem in the source's setting.
It asks whether the existence of such an algorithm would refute the Exponential Time Hypothesis.
Known connections to the stronger SETH assumption do not automatically establish that implication.
Proving it would ground a basic fine-grained lower bound in a weaker assumption and clarify the role of limited nondeterminism in polynomial-time hardness.
